estBinSize

Source: R/pb_helpers.R
estBinSize.Rd

estBinSize() estimates the number of bins for discretizing a continuous variable with one of the rules "Freedman.Diaconis", "Sqrt", "Sturges", "Rice", "Doane" and "Scott.Normal".

estBinSize(time_vector, nPoints, drop_fac, bin_method)

Arguments

time_vector

A numeric vector. The time series data points that need to be binned.

nPoints

An integer. The total number of data points in time_vector.

drop_fac

A numeric. A factor to adjust the estimated number of bins: the number of bins given by the rule is multiplied by this value. Values below 1 give fewer, wider bins, which helps when the rule gives too many empty bins.

bin_method

A character string. The rule that estimates the number of bins. Possible values include "Freedman.Diaconis", "Sqrt", "Sturges", "Rice", "Doane", and "Scott.Normal". See details.

Value

A number: the number of bins given by the rule, multiplied by drop_fac. It is not rounded; sc.squeeze() rounds it up with ceiling().

Details

With n the number of points (nPoints), the rules give:

"Freedman.Diaconis"

bins of width 2 IQR / n^(1/3), with IQR the interquartile range of the points (Freedman and Diaconis, 1981).

"Sqrt"

sqrt(n) bins.

"Sturges"

log2(n) + 1 bins (Sturges, 1926).

"Rice"

2 n^(1/3) bins.

"Doane"

1 + log2(n) + log2(1 + |g| / s) bins, with g the sample skewness of the points and s = sqrt(6 (n - 2) / ((n + 1) (n + 3))) (Doane, 1976).

"Scott.Normal"

bins of width 3.49 sd / n^(1/3), with sd the standard deviation of the points, for nearly normal data (Scott, 1979).

Freedman-Diaconis and Scott give a bin width, which is turned into a number of bins by dividing the range of the points by it. Their width is 0 when the interquartile range or the standard deviation is 0 (when the points are all equal, or for Freedman-Diaconis when their first and third quartiles are equal) and undefined for Scott with a single point; the rule then gives one bin, with a message. The number of bins of every rule is multiplied by drop_fac.

References

Doane, D. P. (1976). Aesthetic frequency classifications. The American Statistician, 30, 181-183.

Freedman, D. and Diaconis, P. (1981). On the histogram as a density estimator: L2 theory. Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete, 57, 453-476.

Scott, D. W. (1979). On optimal and data-based histograms. Biometrika, 66, 605-610.

Sturges, H. A. (1926). The choice of a class interval. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 21, 65-66.
